answer_1.quote: we introduce TurtleBench, a set of manually crafted image/text to code tasks in turtle geometry to evaluate the abilities of these models to combine visual pattern recognition, mathematical reasoning, Python programming, and abstract geometrical reasoning.
answer_1.outputs: Python Turtle code, Rabbit library code

answer_2.quote: using the OpenCV module in Python, the binary versions of the correct shape and the produced shape are compared using an adjusted measure of bitwise similarity... If the bitwise similarity between output and ground truth is higher than 95% the models' output is labeled as correct and incorrect otherwise.

answer_4.quote: To make sure that our heuristic in labeling the correctness of generated shapes is reliable, we manually annotated 2000 pairs of input and output images and we found that only three instances of pairs were labeled incorrectly (two of them false negative and the other false positive.)
answer_4.guideline: manually annotated 2000 pairs of input and output images
